ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached coordinate-plane images show the standard quadrant convention: Quadrant I is upper-right with x>0 and y>0; Quadrant II is upper-left with x<0 and y>0; Quadrant III is lower-left with x<0 and y<0; Quadrant IV is lower-right with x>0 and y<0. Reasoning: The graph is y=f(x)=-3.5x+7. For Quadrant III, we would need x<0 and y<0. But if x<0, then -3.5x is positive, so y=-3.5x+7 is greater than 7, hence positive. Therefore no point of the graph can lie in Quadrant III. The other quadrants do occur: x=1 gives y=3.5 in Quadrant I; x=-1 gives y=10.5 in Quadrant II; x=3 gives y=-3.5 in Quadrant IV. Thus the only quadrant containing no points is III.

It never goes into the lower-left region, which the image labels quadrant III.
